claim: In the matching retail DLL, FormAnimator.ReqSlotAnm (0x06004E70) is a 722-byte method taking SkillSlotEnum skill_slot, Boolean rev, Int32 def_pl_idx, and Boolean atk_side. It reads the equipped skill-slot id and SkillSlotData; conditionally reverses the host and def_pl_idx Player directions only when rev and isCopiedOpponentDir are both true; applies a numeric skill_slot 86/87/88/89 exception to Status3/isAddedDownTimeByPerformance clearing; unconditionally calls Player.ChangeState with literal 10; takes an early weapon-override branch when weaponIdx and SkillSlotData.weaponAnm are both nonnegative, where it selects a weapon animation, calls ReqBasicAnm(result,false,-1), increments weaponAtkCnt and returns; otherwise it writes AnmReqType=1, SkillSlotID=skill_slot, calls InitAnmWork, returns immediately when atk_side is false, and when atk_side is true performs the exact fatigue/skill-attribute/preserve-last-skill/evaluation/S1-reset tail recorded in the provenance summary. In verified R6 raw capture bytes, all 717 PRE calls pair with POST calls and all 717 directly contain Player.ChangeState with recorder argument NormalAnm. Fourteen calls additionally contain nested ReqBasicAnm and 703 do not. The observed parent/argument split is exact: 262 StartOpponentAnm-parented calls are rev=false, def_pl_idx=-1, atk_side=false; 36 StartSlotAnm_Immediately-parented calls are rev=true, def_pl_idx=recorded target, atk_side=true; and 419 recorder-root calls are atk_side=true, of which 316 are rev=false/def=-1 and 103 are rev=true/def=recorded target.
